sections.heading: Is Spray Foaming Your Roof a Good Idea?

runs.v: A sound, dry low-slope roof on commercial buildings or a flat residential section gains continuous insulation, air sealing, and a seamless waterproofing layer in one step. Closed-cell spray foam acts as both insulation and a moisture barrier, spray foam creates a continuous insulation layer reducing heat loss in winter, and properly installed spray foam roofing can reduce the workload on heating and cooling systems, so spray foam roofing can lower utility bills and reduce energy costs significantly; that thermal performance is the source of its energy savings. Seamless waterproofing reduces the risk of leaks from heavy rain and snow, foam roofs can provide superior moisture protection compared to traditional roofs, and by holding a uniform roof temperature, spray foam can help prevent ice dams. The rigid, fully adhered layer of cured spray foam can also add structural integrity, and a properly maintained foam roof can last anywhere from 20 to over 50 years; spray foam roofs can last over 50 years with proper maintenance and periodic recoats.

c.v: Can spray foam be applied to a roof?

runs.v: Yes: spray foam roofing systems can be applied over existing roofs, including most existing roof assemblies, and over concrete, wood, or metal decks once the substrate passes a moisture test, and spray foam easily molds around vents and uneven surfaces, filling the gaps around penetrations that other systems flash by hand. Foam roofs are a poor match for a steep pitched house roof covered in shingles or slate, where the foam cannot shed water the way the original covering does.

sections.heading: Spray Foam Roofing vs. Spray Foam Insulation and Attic Insulation

runs.v: and spray foam roofing share a chemistry but not a job. Foam insulation work sprays open- or closed-cell polyurethane spray foam insulation inside walls, attics, and foundations, where spray foam insulation provides superior air sealing and creates an airtight thermal barrier: it effectively seals gaps and cracks in buildings, and air sealing can improve indoor temperature consistency and limit outdoor air infiltration. Spray foam insulation offers higher thermal resistance than fiberglass, with a higher R-value than fiberglass or cellulose, it can reduce energy costs significantly, and spray foam insulation can last over 50 years with proper care. Attic insulation goes under the roof deck, while spray foam roofing goes on top of the deck or the existing roof, where it must also shed water and carry a coating for protection. Montclair homeowners who want both should have the roof made dry and sound first, because interior foam cannot protect a house from a roof that still leaks.
